# OpenProgram 1.6.0 Release Notes

OpenProgram 1.6.0 updates itself inside the App, downloading only what changed; connects dozens of coding agents and AI apps to OpenProgram's models through its gateway; runs chats on Gemini CLI beside Codex, Claude Code and DeepSeek Harness, and brings their pictures and projects into synced conversations; and redraws the phone app with iOS's own menus and gestures. Which packages this release carries is listed under "Download and installation".

## ✨ New features

- **Updates inside the App, only what changed.** From 1.6.0 on, the App looks for an update 30 seconds after it starts and then every hour, downloads in the background only the files that changed (code, runtime, or the App itself), builds and tries the new version, and holds it behind the NEW badge; **Restart to update** swaps it in. A new App shell is assembled beside the running App from its unchanged files and its signature is checked before the swap. An update that fails to build or start leaves the current version running, and **Go back to a previous version** picks any version kept on the computer. You hear of an update only when a release is published.
- **Your coding agents on OpenProgram's models.** Settings connects dozens of agents and apps to OpenProgram's gateway, among them Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Codex, OpenCode, Gemini CLI, Antigravity, Cursor CLI, Copilot CLI, Qwen Code, Cline, Droid, Crush, Goose, Kimi Code, Pi, Zed, VS Code, JetBrains IDEs, Obsidian, Raycast and Cherry Studio. Each gets a key of its own and OpenProgram's models with their efforts in its own config, follows changes to the model list, a moved port or a new key, and on disconnect gets back exactly what you had, your own entries and edits included.
- **More of each agent, configured from its card.** Claude Code runs OpenProgram's models in its own chats with a subagents model also used by Explore and Plan, and each Claude Code config folder is a row of its own; Claude Desktop can run as a separate "Claude OpenProgram" copy beside your signed-in one; Codex gets subagent and memories models, an OpenProgram-only profile and Background Compaction; typing `agy` in a terminal starts Antigravity on OpenProgram's model; Cursor CLI and Devin pick among their own models.
- **A gateway that speaks more APIs.** The gateway also serves Responses over WebSocket, `/responses/compact`, Google's Gemini API, the Ollama API and model metadata, and answers a web search an agent asks for with OpenProgram's own search when the model has none.
- **Chats on Gemini CLI.** The Harness chip runs a conversation on Google's Gemini CLI with your Google sign-in or Gemini API key, with its models, tool cards, approvals, Stop, token use and a session per branch, as Codex, Claude Code and DeepSeek Harness do.
- **Claude Code chats feel native.** Claude Code's commands, edits and checklists show as OpenProgram's own cards, its plan is approved as written, and its questions appear on OpenProgram's question card. Without a sign-in of its own, Claude Code runs on the Anthropic API key in Model Services, and a new sign-in or key takes effect at the next turn.
- **Synced conversations land where they belong.** A conversation synced from Codex, the Claude app or DeepSeek Harness goes into the project of its folder instead of the home project, and pictures you sent in Claude Code or Codex show where they were sent. Your messages reach these agents exactly as you typed them.
- **Continue in the agent's own app.** Codex, Claude Code and DeepSeek Harness close their process when a turn ends, so the Codex app, the Claude app or DeepSeek Harness can go on with the same thread instead of saying it is open elsewhere.
- **Codex asks you.** Codex's own questions and its requests for more access appear on cards with Codex's reason, attached images reach Codex and Claude Code, and Codex conversations carry ChatGPT's mark.
- **The phone app, redrawn.** Menus are iOS's own: a long press on a chat or a message lifts it with its actions, and a project's … menu offers Pin, Rename and Archive chats. Pages push and swipe back as on iOS, a chat row swipes to Pin or Archive, and the computer button grows into a menu of your paired computers.
- **A Neutral look by default.** White and graphite, following the system's light or dark mode, on the web, the desktop App and the phone.
- **Outside agents in the sidebar.** A conversation running in Codex, Claude Code or another outside agent shows that agent's logo in the status slot, breathing while a turn runs, with a corner dot for unread, waiting for you or failed.
- **Suggested next message, more often.** It also appears when you come back to a chat that finished in the background, and for chats idle up to 48 hours.

## 🐞 Bug fixes

- **Retries and stops in Codex stay in one thread.** A failed or stopped Codex turn keeps the conversation in its thread, so the next turn or a retry goes on there and nothing is handed over twice.
- **Claude Code is never interrupted** by an answer to a request it had already withdrawn or settled, and the next turn waits for the previous process to close instead of resuming a copy of the session.
- **Effort goes as chosen.** A harness conversation shows effort levels once its harness is read and sends only a level the model takes; Off and Ultra on an OpenProgram model run through Codex turn thinking off and go to the highest level.
- **Chinese, Japanese and Korean text** shows on an iPhone instead of boxed question marks.
- **Signing in from a link** lands on the chat list with your theme applied.
- **A conversation on a provider that is gone** falls back to the last model you used instead of failing.
- **Synced conversations** never move into a project you removed or one on another machine, and a failing placement backs off instead of retrying on every check.
- **Nothing hangs or races.** A run whose model stream dies unexpectedly ends with the error instead of waiting forever, and Jobs and conversation writes no longer race each other.

## 🚀 Improvements

- **Small updates.** A one-line change downloads about 11 KB; a re-signed App costs 21 MB instead of 291 MB, because large files travel as pieces and only changed pieces are fetched.
- **Smaller installers.** The macOS DMG is 420 MB instead of 729 MB, and the runtime leaves out package test suites, debug symbols and Git's Credential Manager.
- **Subscriptions go through the vendors' own programs.** Codex, Copilot, Gemini and SuperGrok subscriptions are used through those programs instead of OpenProgram signing in to them, and Codex plan limits are read from Codex itself.
- **Your settings stay safe when agents connect.** Each agent's key is derived from the gateway key without revealing it, key files are readable only by you, and a damaged undo record makes disconnect refuse instead of forgetting your original settings.
- **The Harness menu** greys a harness that cannot start or has no models and says why, and shows a change of sign-in at once.
- **The phone app opens fast** with the last chat list at cold start, one shared connection and a reconnect on wake, and changes page without a jump.
- **Smoother composer.** The composer's slide runs at full frame rate.
- **Logos in dark themes.** The Codex logo is drawn without its white tile on a dark theme, and the iOS app icon keeps its colours in dark mode.

On macOS, open the DMG and copy `OpenProgram.app` to `/Applications`. On Windows, run the installer; it installs for your user only. The release manifest lists the SHA-256 of every file. A file whose name ends in `-unsigned` was built without a publisher signature; see "Unsigned packages" below when that applies.

### CLI / Server

Install this release on macOS or Linux; the installer selects the architecture and verifies the runtime:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://fzkuji.github.io/OpenProgram/install | OPENPROGRAM_VERSION=1.6.0 sh
```

On Windows x64, in PowerShell:

```powershell
irm https://fzkuji.github.io/OpenProgram/install.ps1 | iex
```

## 🔄 Upgrade guide

- **Desktop:** from this version on, the App downloads a new release in the background and **Restart to update** beside the NEW badge installs it. To look sooner: Settings → Versions and Updates → Check now.
- **Desktop on macOS:** open the DMG and replace the application in `/Applications`.
- **Desktop on Linux:** install the AppImage or deb above in place of the old one. A deb takes a newer App shell as a deb; everything else updates inside the App.
- **Desktop on Windows:** run the installer above; it installs over the existing App and keeps your data.
- **CLI / Server:** run `openprogram upgrade`, or repeat the versioned installation command above.
- **Your data:** configuration, conversations, Programs, and saved progress under `~/.openprogram` are preserved.
- **After upgrading:** check `openprogram --version`.

See the [upgrade guide](https://github.com/Fzkuji/OpenProgram/blob/v1.6.0/docs/install/upgrade.html) for details.
